body:
Dev Patel: Heads up: prepping Support for Suggestions (Optimize) beta. Can folks drop anticipated customer questions + suggested canned responses? Biggest ones I’m hearing: “why is risk HIGH?”, “why did savings change week-to-week?”, “why do I see no suggestions?”

Rachel Kim: +1. Enterprise CS asked for something they can paste into emails. Also: “Can you guarantee savings?” and “Can we apply it automatically?”

Miguel Santos: From onboarding calls: “Does High risk mean it will break prod?” They want concrete reasons, not just the label.

Aparna Reddy: Mid-market: “The savings number went DOWN after we enabled caching… did we mess up?” Also “Why does it say insufficient telemetry when we have traffic?”

Liam O'Rourke: TAM angle: “Is the estimate per-route or org-wide?” and “Does this include Dedicated vs Hosted differences?”

Evan Scott: Also: “Does showing me these suggestions leak usage patterns to other teams?” (RBAC / audit log question)

Dev Patel: Great. Drafting canned responses here; please poke holes.

Dev Patel: Q: “Why is risk HIGH?”
A (draft): Risk is an automated classification based on the likelihood the change could impact latency/quality/SLOs and how reversible it is. High risk doesn’t mean “don’t do it,” it means “validate carefully.” Open the suggestion details to see the specific rationale (e.g., low latency headroom, high workload variance, low confidence in cache hit-rate) and the assumptions used. For beta, we recommend testing in a lower environment or a small canary, and monitoring p95 latency + key quality metrics before broad rollout.

Dev Patel: Q: “The risk label is vague—what exactly drove it?”
A (draft): In the details drawer, we include a “Risk rationale” section with the top drivers and what they mean (ex: “p95 latency headroom < X%”, “traffic variance high”, “telemetry window too small”). If the rationale is missing/doesn’t match observed behavior, we can escalate to Optimize to review calibration.

Markus Klein: Can we add a line like “risk is scoped to the target (route/model/region) not global”? Customers assume it’s across their whole account.

Dev Patel: Good call, adding.

Dev Patel: Q: “Why did savings change week-to-week?”
A (draft): Savings estimates are based on recent baselines (traffic mix, token usage, latency, cacheability signals) over a rolling window. If your usage patterns shift (prompt lengths, peak concurrency, model mix), the estimate will change. During beta, treat savings as directional and review the “Basis of estimate” section for the data window and inputs. If numbers swing dramatically without any traffic change, we’ll investigate telemetry freshness/attribution.

Aparna Reddy: Can we be explicit that the UI isn’t “retroactively tracking realized savings” yet? People assume it’s reporting actual savings.

Dev Patel: Yep. Adding disclaimer: estimate ≠ guaranteed, not a bill credit.

Selene Huang: +1. Also mention: we intentionally suppress suggestions if we see elevated regression signals (quality/latency) OR if confidence is too low. So sometimes suggestions disappear even if they existed last week.

Dev Patel: Q: “Why do I have no suggestions?”
A (draft): Common reasons:
1) Not enough eligible traffic for the route/model to compute a reliable baseline.
2) Telemetry is delayed/stale (estimates require recent token metering + request metrics).
3) Suggestions are suppressed due to guardrails (risk/quality/latency signals).
4) Filters applied (route/model/region) are too narrow.
5) Beta not enabled for the workspace, or missing permission.
Troubleshooting: confirm you’re on the right workspace, clear filters, verify you can see usage dashboards, and check that the route has sustained traffic in the last 24–72h. If still empty, share workspace + route + model with Support and we’ll check telemetry freshness.

Miguel Santos: Add quick “what to send Support” checklist: tenant/workspace id, route name, model, region, time window.

Dev Patel: Adding.

Liam O'Rourke: Q: “Is this estimate per-route or for my whole spend?”
A: The list shows suggestions scoped to a specific target (route + model + region). The drawer shows both unit savings (e.g., $/1M tokens) and an estimated monthly impact for that target based on recent volume.

Jonas Weber: Please avoid saying “based on last 30 days” universally. Some tenants are using shorter windows depending on data availability. Better: “recent rolling window shown in Basis of estimate.”

Dev Patel: Noted.

Evan Scott: Q: “Can you guarantee savings / is this a commitment?”
A: No—these are estimates intended to guide optimization. Realized savings depend on workload behavior and safe configuration. We provide the assumptions and inputs used so you can validate, and we recommend monitoring after changes.

Rachel Kim: Also: “Can I apply this with one click?”
A: For beta, read-only: we’re validating estimates + guardrails before enabling apply workflows. You can still make the underlying config changes manually; we can share guidance if needed.

Marissa Cole: +1; and we should be consistent: “read-only beta” is the phrase we’re using in launch brief.

Dev Patel: Q: “Does this affect my latency / quality?”
A: It can. That’s why we provide a risk level and rationale. Low risk suggestions are expected to be safe for most workloads, but you should still validate. Medium/high risk suggestions should be tested with canaries and monitored against your SLOs.

Selene Huang: Can we add “If you see quality regressions, revert immediately; this is reversible” for caching/batching recs.

Dev Patel: Adding.

Evan Scott: Security/RBAC question:
Q: “Who can see Suggestions? Does it expose sensitive usage?”
A (draft): Access is controlled by Console RBAC. Viewing Suggestions is read-only and scoped to your workspace. Access is audit logged. The UI surfaces cost/usage-derived metrics at an aggregate level for optimization; it does not expose raw prompts/responses.

Rachel Kim: Please add: “If your org requires stricter controls, we can scope the permission to admin roles only.” Enterprise loves that line.

Dev Patel: Q: “Why does it say ‘insufficient telemetry’ when we have traffic?”
A: The Suggestions pipeline requires specific telemetry (token metering + request metrics) for the relevant route/model/region and a minimum volume threshold. If telemetry is delayed, missing tags, or the route is new, the UI may show insufficient telemetry. We can verify ingestion/freshness and confirm whether the route is properly attributed.

Aparna Reddy: This one is happening a lot. Can we give an ETA statement?

Dev Patel: Maybe: “Telemetry generally updates within <N hours; if it’s been >24h, contact Support.” I’ll confirm with Logan/telemetry team before we promise.

Supportbot: :memo: Reminder: Please don’t request or share customer prompt content in Slack. Use workspace ID + route/model/region only.

Markus Klein: Another FAQ: “Why do I see a batching suggestion AND a caching suggestion—do savings double count?”

Aditya Rao: Good one. Answer should be: savings are computed to avoid double-counting; when multiple suggestions apply, each estimate is against a consistent baseline and the UI calls out interactions in the drawer. If a customer suspects overlap, we can review their specific case.

Dev Patel: Adding.

Dev Patel: Proposed final canned snippets (paste-ready). If you’re ok with these, I’ll move them into the Support FAQ doc.

Dev Patel: 1) Risk HIGH snippet:
“High risk means the change has a higher chance of impacting latency/quality/SLOs for the specific route/model/region, or the estimate has lower confidence. It doesn’t mean ‘unsafe by default,’ but it does mean you should validate via canary and monitoring. Open the suggestion to see the specific risk drivers and assumptions.”

Dev Patel: 2) Savings changed snippet:
“Estimates are computed from a recent rolling baseline. If your traffic mix, prompt lengths, concurrency, or model mix changes, the projected savings can change week-to-week. Use the ‘Basis of estimate’ section to see the window and inputs. Treat beta savings as directional, not guaranteed.”

Dev Patel: 3) No suggestions snippet:
“If you don’t see suggestions, it usually means (a) there isn’t enough eligible traffic to compute a reliable baseline, (b) telemetry is delayed/stale for that route/model/region, (c) guardrails suppressed suggestions due to elevated risk/regression signals, (d) filters are narrowing the view, or (e) beta/permissions aren’t enabled. If you share workspace ID + route + model + region + timeframe, we can help debug.”

Rachel Kim: Looks good. Can we include a 1-liner for “How do I give feedback?”

Dev Patel: Yep: “Use the in-product feedback link or reply with suggestion ID(s) + what you expected; we track this weekly with Product/Eng.”

Marissa Cole: Please emphasize “suggestion ID” for tracking. It’s in the drawer header.

Dev Patel: Done. I’ll post the FAQ draft in the Support folder and tag @Rachel Kim @Miguel Santos @Aparna Reddy for review. Also looping @Jonas Weber for sign-off on risk wording.
